intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026

selected_hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Explore Djemaa el-Fna Square
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech at this UNESCO-listed square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, acrobats, and musicians perform as the sun sets. Sample street food like harira soup, msemen flatbread, and freshly squeezed orange juice from the surrounding stalls.

experiences.name: Camel Trek and Overnight Desert Camp in Erg Chebbi
experiences.description: Ride a camel into the towering golden dunes of the Sahara at sunset, then spend the night in a traditional Berber camp under a canopy of stars. Enjoy a campfire dinner with tagine and mint tea, listen to Gnawa music, and wake up to a breathtaking desert sunrise.

experiences.name: Guided Tour of the Medina and Souks
experiences.description: Navigate the labyrinthine medieval alleyways of Marrakech's ancient Medina with a knowledgeable local guide. Discover the vibrant souks selling spices, leather goods, ceramics, and textiles. Visit the historic Medersa Ben Youssef, a stunning 14th-century Islamic college adorned with intricate zellige tilework and carved cedar wood.

experiences.name: Visit Bahia Palace and El Badi Palace Ruins
experiences.description: Step back in time exploring two of Marrakech's most iconic historical landmarks. Bahia Palace dazzles with ornate Moroccan craftsmanship, painted ceilings, and lush courtyards. Nearby, the haunting ruins of El Badi Palace — once one of the world's most magnificent palaces — offer a powerful glimpse into the Saadian dynasty's grandeur.

experiences.name: Sandboarding on the Sahara Dunes
experiences.description: Get your adrenaline pumping by sandboarding down the massive rust-colored dunes of Erg Chebbi. Local operators provide boards and brief instruction, making it accessible for beginners. Combine with a quad biking session across the desert flats for a full adventure morning before the midday heat sets in.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take the 19 bus or negotiate a petit taxi (~50–70 MAD) to your riad in the Medina near Djemaa el-Fna. Check in, freshen up, and orient yourself with a short walk through the surrounding alleyways.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle first explore of Djemaa el-Fna square and its surroundings. Watch snake charmers, musicians, and henna artists from a distance (no obligation to pay). Stroll into the northern souks briefly to get your bearings — carpets, spices, leather goods. Visit the free exterior of the Koutoubia Mosque (the tallest landmark in Marrakech) just a 5-minute walk from the square.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Djemaa el-Fna as dusk falls — the square transforms into a massive open-air food market. Grab a numbered stall dinner: harira soup, merguez sausages, and fresh-squeezed orange juice. Sit on the terrace of Café de France or Café Argana for a free panoramic view of the buzzing square with a mint tea.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a coffee and msemen (Moroccan flatbread) from a street cart near the airport or riad for ~10 MAD
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a quick sandwich from a medina snack stall (~15–20 MAD) after check-in
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls — harira soup (5 MAD), merguez plate (30 MAD), fresh orange juice (4 MAD). Full meal under 50 MAD (~$5)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or a bureau de change in the Medina (avoid hotels). Keep small bills for stalls and taxis. Agree on taxi fares BEFORE getting in. Stay hydrated — March can be warm (~20–25°C).

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Bahia Palace (entrance ~70 MAD / ~$7) — a stunning 19th-century palace with ornate Moorish courtyards, carved cedar ceilings, and tiled rooms. Arrive before 9:30 AM to beat crowds. Afterward, explore the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) next door — the old synagogue and market are fascinating and mostly free to wander.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entrance ~70 MAD) — one of the most beautiful Islamic schools in North Africa, dating to the 14th century. The carved stucco, zellij tilework, and central pool are breathtaking. Nearby, pop into the Museum of Marrakech in the same complex (combo ticket available ~120 MAD). Explore the Mouassine neighborhood's quieter souks for artisan workshops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Medina souks for golden-hour shopping — practice your bargaining (start at 30–40% of the asking price). Pick up argan oil, spices, or leather goods. Dinner at a local restaurant just off the main square.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your riad if included, or a street-side café: khobz bread, olive oil, amlou (almond-argan paste), mint tea (~20–30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Cheap local eatery near Ben Youssef: tagine of the day with bread (~40–50 MAD)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Chez Lamine (famous for mechoui roasted lamb) near Djemaa el-Fna — half portion mechoui + bread ~60–80 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Ben Youssef Madrasa and Bahia Palace are the two unmissable historic sites in Marrakech — don't skip them. Wear modest clothing (covered shoulders and knees) out of respect. Photography inside palaces may require a small fee.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Majorelle Garden and Yves Saint Laurent Museum area. The Majorelle Garden (entrance ~150 MAD) is a cobalt-blue botanical oasis — iconic and worth the splurge. The adjacent Berber Museum is included in the ticket. Arrive at opening (8:00 AM) to avoid tour groups.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a petit taxi to the Saadian Tombs (entrance ~70 MAD) — a 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917, with intricately decorated mausoleums. Nearby, visit El Badi Palace ruins (entrance ~70 MAD) — a vast 16th-century palace now in romantic decay, with rooftop stork nests and panoramic views. Both are within 10 minutes of each other.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class or hammam experience. A budget hammam (traditional steam bath) at a local public hammam costs just 15–25 MAD — ask your riad to recommend a neighborhood one. Alternatively, book an affordable cooking class (~200–300 MAD) through your riad or a local host to learn to make tagine and couscous.

meals.breakfast: Café near Majorelle: café au lait + croissant or msemen (~25 MAD)
meals.lunch: Picnic from the market — olives, bread, cheese, fruit from the Mellah market (~30 MAD total)
meals.dinner: Riad home-cooked meal if your accommodation offers it, or a neighborhood restaurant: vegetable couscous Friday-style (~50 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle is the priciest attraction but genuinely spectacular. Budget travelers can view the exterior walls and the surrounding Gueliz neighborhood for free if needed. Book the hammam visit in the evening after dusty sightseeing — it's deeply refreshing.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (6:00–7:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert via a shared budget CTM bus or a booked budget group tour van to Merzouga (~10–11 hours total with stops). The route passes through the dramatic High Atlas Mountains — snow-capped peaks in March. Stop at the Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) for photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa') — if on a self-arranged bus, stop for 1–2 hours to see the exterior of Aït Benhaddou UNESCO kasbah from the roadside or pay ~30 MAD entry. Continue through the Draa Valley — date palms, mud-brick kasbahs, and desert vistas. Arrive in Merzouga village by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a budget desert camp or guesthouse in Merzouga (~150–250 MAD per night). At sunset, mount a dromedary camel for a 1-hour ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes (negotiate ~100–150 MAD per person with your camp). Watch the sunset paint the dunes gold and red from atop the highest dune. Sleep under the stars at a basic desert camp.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at riad before departure (~20–30 MAD or included)
meals.lunch: Roadside stop in the Atlas or Ouarzazate: tagine at a local restaurant (~40–50 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner included at most desert camps — traditional Berber tagine and mint tea around a campfire (~included in camp fee or ~80 MAD extra)

day_by_day.notes: Book transport in advance: CTM bus Marrakech–Ouarzazate–Merzouga (~120–180 MAD one way) or join a budget group tour (400–600 MAD all-in including camel ride and camp). March nights in the desert can drop to 5–10°C — bring a warm layer. The camp will provide blankets.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) to climb the Erg Chebbi dunes for the sunrise — one of the most magical experiences in Morocco. The shifting orange light on the sand is extraordinary. Take photos, meditate, or simply absorb the silence. Return to camp for a Berber breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Merzouga village on foot or by bicycle (rent for ~30–50 MAD/day). Visit the local Gnawa musicians' quarter — this desert town is famous for its traditional Gnawa music. Optionally, visit a local Berber family for tea (arranged through your guesthouse — free or small tip). Explore the edge of the dunes on foot — the Erg Chebbi dune field stretches 22km.
day_by_day.evening: Optional sandboarding on the dunes (boards rentable from camp ~30–50 MAD). Begin the return journey or spend a second night. If returning: take an afternoon/evening bus back toward Ouarzazate, or arrange a shared taxi. Alternatively, enjoy another night under the stars — highly recommended.

meals.breakfast: Berber camp breakfast: khobz, olive oil, honey, eggs, mint tea (included in camp or ~30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Local Merzouga restaurant: camel meat tagine or chicken tagine (~50–60 MAD) — a rare local specialty
meals.dinner: Camp dinner or local guesthouse: lentil soup + tagine + fresh bread (~60–80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise dune climb is the highlight of the entire trip — set multiple alarms. Bring sunscreen and a scarf to wrap around your face against wind-blown sand. Stay hydrated. If you want to extend desert time, a second night is very affordable and deeply restorative.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Merzouga early morning back toward Marrakech. If budget allows, stop at Aït Benhaddou UNESCO World Heritage kasbah (entry ~30 MAD) — a spectacular fortified mud-brick city used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Cross the Draa Valley again and enjoy the changing landscapes from desert to mountain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by mid-to-late afternoon. Drop bags at riad and recover. Visit any missed Medina spots: the spice souk (Rahba Kedima square), the dyers' souk, or the leather tanneries (best viewed from nearby leather shop rooftops — tip the shop owner ~10–20 MAD for access). The tanneries are a vivid, pungent, unforgettable sight.
day_by_day.evening: Final big evening in Marrakech. Splurge slightly on a sit-down dinner at a mid-range Moroccan restaurant (still budget-friendly). Afterward, return to Djemaa el-Fna for a final evening of people-watching, storytellers, and musicians — soak it all in.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at camp or guesthouse before departure
meals.lunch: Roadside stop en route: harira soup + sandwich (~30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Nomad (Rahba Kedima area) or similar — modern Moroccan cuisine, mains ~80–120 MAD. Or splurge on a set menu at a traditional riad restaurant (~150 MAD for 3 courses)

day_by_day.notes: The return journey is long (10–11 hours). Bring snacks, water, a book, and a power bank. If you booked a group tour, the return is organized. Independent travelers: book CTM bus tickets in advance at the Merzouga bus stop or online. Aït Benhaddou stop may require a detour — confirm with your driver.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech. Explore any last corners of the Medina: the Mouassine Fountain area, the Chrob ou Chouf Fountain (beautiful carved cedar canopy), or simply wander the quiet morning alleyways before the crowds arrive. Visit the weekly Mellah market for fresh produce, olives, and spices to take home as gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks — leather slippers (babouches), argan oil, ras el hanout spice blend, hand-painted ceramics. Bargain confidently. Pack your bags, check out of the riad (store luggage if needed), and take a final mint tea on a rooftop café overlooking the Medina.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Marrakech Menara Airport (allow 45–60 minutes from the Medina, including taxi time). Reflect on an incredible week of mountains, desert, culture, and history. Departure.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at riad or street café: beghrir (honeycomb pancakes) with honey and butter + mint tea (~25 MAD)
meals.lunch: Quick medina lunch: msemen filled with kefta (ground meat) from a street stall (~20–25 MAD), or a bowl of bissara (fava bean soup) with bread (~10 MAD) — a Marrakchi staple
meals.dinner: Airport or early dinner before departure: keep it light and simple

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 7 days (excluding flights): Accommodation ~1,000–1,400 MAD | Transport ~400–600 MAD | Entry fees ~500–600 MAD | Food ~700–900 MAD | Camel + desert activities ~200–300 MAD. TOTAL: approximately 2,800–3,800 MAD (~$280–$380 USD) for the full week. Morocco is one of the world's best-value destinations — always carry small change and enjoy haggling as part of the cultural experience.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to your boutique riad in the Medina near Djemaa el-Fna (approx. 20–30 min by taxi, ~80–100 MAD). Check in, freshen up, and rest briefly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk around Djemaa el-Fna square and the surrounding souks. Explore the nearby spice market (Rahba Kedima) and the dyers' souk at a relaxed pace. Pick up a hand-drawn map from your riad host for context.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the rooftop terrace of Café de France or Café Argana overlooking Djemaa el-Fna to watch the square come alive — snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians fill the space at dusk. Stroll back through the square after dark to soak in the electric atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eaten on the plane or grab a light snack (msemen flatbread and mint tea) from a street stall near the riad upon arrival (~20 MAD)
meals.lunch: Quick and authentic lunch at Chez Lamine near Djemaa el-Fna — try the slow-cooked lamb mechoui sandwich (~60–80 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Marrakchi restaurant overlooking the square — classic Moroccan tagine (chicken with preserved lemon or lamb with prunes) and fresh-squeezed orange juice (~150–200 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Keep the evening leisurely — jet lag may set in. Drink bottled water and avoid raw street food until your stomach adjusts. Exchange currency at the airport or a nearby bureau de change (avoid hotel rates).

day_by_day.morning: Full morning at the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior only for non-Muslims) and then visit the Saadian Tombs — a stunning 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917. Book tickets in advance (~70 MAD). Arrive early (9:00 AM) to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Bahia Palace (14th–19th century), one of the finest examples of Moroccan architecture with intricate zellige tilework and carved cedar ceilings (~70 MAD entry). Afterward, wander through the mellah (historic Jewish quarter) and visit the Lazama Synagogue.
day_by_day.evening: Take a cooking class at a local riad school (several offered near the Medina, ~300–400 MAD per person). Learn to make harira soup, a classic tagine, and bastilla. The class typically includes dinner — a wonderful cultural and culinary immersion.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your riad (usually included) — expect msemen, amlou (argan-almond dip), fresh fruit, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad restaurant in the Medina — modern Moroccan cuisine, rooftop views, great for people-watching (~120–160 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner is part of the cooking class experience — enjoy what you've made (~included in class fee)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Medina streets are uneven cobblestone. The Saadian Tombs can get crowded by 10:30 AM, so aim to arrive right at opening. Bahia Palace is a 15-min walk from the tombs.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Yves Saint Laurent Museum (Musée YSL Marrakech) and the adjacent Jardin Majorelle — a stunning cobalt-blue garden that inspired YSL and is now one of Morocco's most visited sites (~200 MAD combined entry). Arrive at 9:00 AM sharp before tour groups arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Musée de Marrakech housed in the 19th-century Mnebhi Palace — beautiful architecture and rotating art exhibitions (~50 MAD). Then head to Ben Youssef Medersa, a 14th-century Quranic school with breathtaking Andalusian-Moroccan craftsmanship (~70 MAD). Both are within walking distance of each other.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at a rooftop bar — try Sky Bar at the Es Saadi hotel or the rooftop at Kozybar near the Mellah for cocktails and panoramic Atlas Mountain views. Then a relaxed evening stroll through the lit-up Djemaa el-Fna.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your riad
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café du Livre (near Gueliz area) or grab street food near the Majorelle garden — try a fresh orange juice and a kefta sandwich (~40–70 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dar Moha — upscale but mid-range accessible, set in a stunning riad with live Gnawa music; prix-fixe Moroccan menu (~250–350 MAD per person). Reserve ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Jardin Majorelle fills up fast — an early start is essential. The garden is a 15-min taxi ride from the Medina (30–40 MAD). The YSL Museum is directly adjacent. Bring a camera — the blue architecture is iconic.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (6:30–7:00 AM) by private shared transfer or organized tour toward the Sahara Desert via the dramatic Draa Valley and Dadès Gorge. The drive passes through the High Atlas Mountains — stop at Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m) for photos and a Berber tea break.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa') — brief stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou ksar, a fortified mud-brick village used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones (~10 MAD entry). Continue driving southeast toward Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi dunes.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Merzouga at dusk (~18:30–19:00). Mount dromedary camels for a 45-minute sunset ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes (included in most tours or ~200–300 MAD separately). Arrive at your desert camp as the stars emerge — one of the most spectacular skies in the world.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your riad before departure — pack snacks for the road
meals.lunch: Lunch stop in Ouarzazate or near Aït Benhaddou — try a roadside restaurant serving harira, tagine, and fresh bread (~80–100 MAD)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — tagine, couscous, and Moroccan salads around a campfire with live Gnawa drumming (~included in camp package or ~150–200 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest travel day (~8–9 hours of driving). Book a reputable shared or private transfer in advance (shared: ~600–800 MAD per person; private: ~1,500–2,000 MAD for the vehicle). The desert camp should be pre-booked — choose a mid-range camp with private or semi-private tents and proper bathroom facilities.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (5:30 AM) to climb the dunes for a breathtaking Sahara sunrise — the colors shift from deep purple to blazing orange and gold. Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast. Explore the edge of the dune sea on foot or by optional quad bike (~200–300 MAD/hour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the village of Merzouga and the nearby Khamlia village — home to the Gnawa people, descendants of sub-Saharan African slaves, known for their hypnotic spiritual music. Attend an informal music session (~donation appreciated). Optionally visit a fossil shop — the region is rich in trilobite and ammonite fossils.
day_by_day.evening: Second night in the desert camp or begin the return journey depending on your tour package. If staying, enjoy a second evening of stargazing — the Sahara offers near-zero light pollution. Try to identify the Milky Way core (visible in March).

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at camp — khobz bread, olive oil, argan honey, hard-boiled eggs, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch in Merzouga village at a local café — try camel meat tagine, a regional specialty (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Camp dinner again or dine at a local auberge in Merzouga if you've returned to town (~100–150 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Temperatures in the Sahara in March are pleasant during the day (20–28°C) but can drop to 5–10°C at night — bring a warm layer. Sandstorms are rare in March but possible; a scarf or keffiyeh is useful. Charge all devices the night before as camps may have limited power.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Merzouga after breakfast and begin the return journey to Marrakech via the scenic Todra Gorge — a 300-meter-high canyon carved by the Todra River. Stop for a 1–2 hour hike through the gorge floor (easy to moderate difficulty, flat terrain). The towering rose-colored walls are spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Dadès Valley (Valley of Roses) — in mid-March, the roses may just be beginning to bloom. Stop at a local cooperative to see rose water and argan oil production. Continue driving west, stopping at Kelaat M'Gouna for a brief town walk.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech (~20:00–21:00). Check back into your riad. Unwind with a traditional hammam session — book an in-riad hammam or visit a local public hammam (Hammam Dar el-Bacha is excellent, ~150–200 MAD for a full scrub and massage).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at desert camp or auberge before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a roadside restaurant in the Dadès Valley — fresh trout from the river is a local specialty (~100–130 MAD)
meals.dinner: Late dinner near your riad in the Medina — try Haj Mustapha in the souks for an authentic, no-frills Moroccan meal (tagine + bread + tea ~60–80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is approximately 8–9 hours with stops. Todra Gorge is a highlight — don't skip it. If you prefer a shorter drive, you can fly Merzouga to Marrakech via Errachidia airport (check availability), though the scenic drive is highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — visit the Mellah Sunday souk for authentic local shopping (ceramics, leather babouches, argan oil, spices, Berber jewelry). Bargaining is expected and part of the culture — start at 40–50% of the asking price. Pick up last-minute gifts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at your riad's rooftop terrace or visit the Agdal Gardens (historic royal gardens south of the Medina, free entry) for a peaceful final afternoon. Alternatively, book a 1-hour traditional Moroccan massage at a local spa (~200–300 MAD) as a farewell treat.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Marrakech — a celebratory meal at a mid-range restaurant. Enjoy the last views of Djemaa el-Fna at night. Pack and prepare for departure. Arrange airport transfer with your riad (they can usually book a reliable taxi at ~100–120 MAD).

meals.breakfast: Final riad breakfast — savor the mint tea and fresh msemen one last time
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Clock Marrakech — creative Moroccan-international fusion in a beautiful riad setting; try the camel burger (~100–150 MAD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Pepe Nero — elegant Italian-Moroccan fusion in a stunning riad setting; excellent for a special final evening (~200–280 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: If your flight is early on Day 8, confirm your airport taxi the night before. The Medina souks are most vibrant on Sunday mornings — a perfect time for final shopping. Keep 200–300 MAD cash for tips across your stay (riad staff, camel guide, camp staff, tour drivers). Morocco is a tipping culture — 10–15% is appreciated.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to boutique riad in Djemaa el-Fna Medina.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in and settle into your riad. After freshening up, take a leisurely guided orientation walk through the labyrinthine souks of the Medina — explore the spice markets, leather tanneries glimpsed from rooftop terraces, and the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square as it begins to come alive with storytellers and musicians.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the full spectacle of Djemaa el-Fna at dusk — snake charmers, acrobats, and open-air food stalls create a sensory feast. Enjoy a private rooftop aperitif at your riad before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (afternoon arrival)
meals.lunch: Light welcome refreshments and traditional Moroccan mint tea and pastries upon check-in at the riad
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Foundouk — a beautifully restored 18th-century caravanserai offering refined Moroccan cuisine; try the lamb pastilla and slow-cooked tagine with preserved lemon

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Keep the first afternoon relaxed to recover from travel. The riad concierge can assist with tipping etiquette and local currency exchange.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Koutoubia Mosque gardens and the magnificent Bahia Palace — a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan craftsmanship with ornate zellij tilework, carved cedarwood ceilings, and lush courtyards. Continue to the Saadian Tombs, a hidden royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the El Badi Palace ruins — once considered one of the most beautiful palaces in the world — with a private historian guide providing rich context. Afterward, visit the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the vibrant Mellah market for artisan silver jewelry and spices.
day_by_day.evening: Private cooking class in a traditional riad kitchen — learn to prepare harira soup, couscous, and bastilla under the guidance of a master Moroccan chef, followed by dining on what you've prepared.

meals.breakfast: Sumptuous Moroccan breakfast at the riad — msemen flatbreads, amlou (argan oil and almond paste), fresh juices, honey, and Berber omelette
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant in the Medina — contemporary Moroccan cuisine with rooftop views; try the spiced carrot salad and slow-roasted lamb shoulder
meals.dinner: Private in-riad dining experience following the cooking class — your own crafted Moroccan feast paired with Moroccan rosé wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the private historian guide and cooking class through your riad concierge at least 48 hours in advance. Comfortable walking shoes essential for Medina exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Private day excursion to the Majorelle Garden — the iconic cobalt-blue botanical garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent — followed by a visit to the adjacent Berber Museum (Musée Berbère) and the YSL Museum showcasing the designer's Moroccan-inspired collections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive hammam and spa ritual at a premium traditional hammam — black soap scrub, kessa exfoliation, ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage at a luxury wellness center such as Les Bains de Marrakech or the Royal Mansour Spa.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitifs at a rooftop bar in Gueliz (the New City) followed by a premium dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast with fresh fruit platters, Moroccan crepes (baghrir), and argan oil selections
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café du Livre or Pepe Nero in Gueliz — relaxed European-Moroccan fusion with excellent salads and grilled fish
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Tobsil — an intimate, legendary Marrakech restaurant inside a historic riad offering a lavish multi-course Moroccan feast with live Gnawa music; reservation essential

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden can be crowded — arrive early. Hammam appointment should be pre-booked. Le Tobsil requires advance reservation and is cash-only; confirm with concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech by private luxury 4x4 vehicle for the Sahara Desert (Merzouga/Erg Chebbi). Journey takes approximately 8–9 hours with scenic stops — cross the High Atlas Mountains via the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m elevation), stopping at a Berber village for tea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Valley of Roses (Dades Valley) and the lunar Draa Valley — ancient kasbahs, palmeries, and dramatic gorges unfold. Stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou — a breathtaking 11th-century ksar (fortified village) used as a backdrop for films including Gladiator and Game of Thrones.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Merzouga as the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi glow at sunset. Check into a luxury desert camp (e.g., Scarabeo Camp or Erg Chebbi Luxury Camp). Mount private camels for a guided sunset ride into the dunes.

meals.breakfast: Early full Moroccan breakfast at the riad before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a curated stop in Ouarzazate — try Restaurant Accord Majeur for traditional Moroccan tagine and fresh salads
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner under the stars at the luxury desert camp — slow-cooked lamb mechoui, couscous, and fresh salads around a campfire with live Gnawa drumming performance

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day — depart by 07:30 to arrive before sunset. Pack a light layer as Atlas Mountain passes can be cool in March. The private 4x4 with an English-speaking driver-guide is essential for this route.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for a private sunrise camel trek deep into the Erg Chebbi dunes — watch the Sahara ignite in shades of amber and crimson as the sun rises over the endless sea of sand. Optional sandboarding on the highest dunes with a guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to camp for a leisurely brunch. Optional quad biking excursion across the desert landscape. Visit a local Berber nomad family for an authentic cultural exchange and traditional tea ceremony. Explore the small town of Merzouga and its fossil market.
day_by_day.evening: Second night at the luxury desert camp — private stargazing session with a telescope guided by a local astronomer (the Sahara offers some of the world's clearest night skies). Relax around the campfire with Berber musicians.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-dawn snack before sunrise trek; full Berber breakfast (khobz bread, honey, olive oil, eggs, mint tea) upon return to camp
meals.lunch: Leisurely brunch at the luxury camp — mezze spreads, grilled meats, fresh salads, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.dinner: Gourmet dinner at the camp — harira soup, chicken bastilla, grilled lamb chops, and traditional Moroccan sweets with mint tea

day_by_day.notes: Temperatures in the Sahara can drop significantly at night in March — pack a warm layer. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a headscarf for daytime dune activities. Sandboarding and quad bikes should be arranged through the camp.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk in the dunes before departing the desert. Begin the return journey to Marrakech via a different scenic route — travel through the stunning Todra Gorge, a dramatic 300-meter-high limestone canyon perfect for a short guided hike along the riverbed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Dades Gorge (Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs) — stop at the famous 'monkey fingers' rock formations and a restored ksar for a private tour. Visit a cooperative producing rose water and rose oil in the Valley of Roses (peak rose season is April–May but cooperatives operate year-round).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Marrakech by evening. Check back into your riad. Wind down with a relaxing hammam session or rooftop terrace drinks.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at the desert camp before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic stop in Tinghir near the Todra Gorge — traditional Amazigh (Berber) cuisine including tafarnout bread and tagine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dar Yacout — one of Marrakech's most celebrated restaurants, a palatial riad with rooftop cocktails, belly dancing, and an extravagant multi-course Moroccan feast

day_by_day.notes: Another long travel day — approximately 7–8 hours including stops. Todra Gorge walk is easy and highly recommended. Dar Yacout requires advance reservation; smart-casual attire appropriate.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — revisit your favorite souk for last-minute artisan shopping: hand-woven Berber rugs, argan oil products, hand-hammered copper lanterns, and leather babouche slippers. Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa — a stunning 14th-century Islamic college with intricate stucco carvings and a tranquil marble courtyard.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relaxed farewell lunch. Final stroll through Djemaa el-Fna and the surrounding Medina. Optional visit to a local argan oil cooperative for a demonstration and premium product purchases. Private transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. If flight is late evening, enjoy a final sunset cocktail on your riad rooftop terrace.

meals.breakfast: Farewell Moroccan breakfast at the riad — a lavish spread to conclude the journey
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café de France overlooking Djemaa el-Fna for a classic Marrakech atmosphere, or at the rooftop terrace of Terrasse des Épices for refined Moroccan dishes
meals.dinner: Light farewell dinner at the riad or airport lounge depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport transfer and check-in. Confirm private transfer timing with concierge the evening before. Keep valuables and fragile souvenir purchases in hand luggage.
